chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad said: on the authority of Imran ibn Musa, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn al-Abbas ibn Huraysh al-Razi, on the authority of some of our scholars, from al-Tayyib (meaning Ali ibn Muhammad), and from Abu Ja'far al-Jawad (peace be upon them both) that they said:
He who claims that Allah has a body, do not give him the poor-rate, and do not pray behind him.

key_terms.الطَّيِّب: The Purified (title for Ali ibn Muhammad)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying behind someone who believes Allah has a body?
ai.summary: In al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this hadith links the theological concept of *tanzih* (divine transcendence) with practical jurisprudence, declaring that affirming a physical body (*al-jism*) for Allah invalidates one's religious authority. This criterion reflects the early Shia emphasis on *tawhid* as a prerequisite for *fiqh*, ensuring that leaders and recipients of charity adhere to the core doctrine of God's immateriality.
